requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Each board develops a bag-and-box proposal with identifiable materials, a closure concept and outbound/return operation. Across the three boards, both construction and visual identity differ meaningfully; recolouring or relabelling the same structure does not establish a distinct direction.

The specification has two pages and unambiguously names one of the three proposed directions. It records the selected construction for S and M bags and the L box, material family/name and grade, thickness or grammage, mass targets, usable and closed external dimensions, actual blank dimensions, fold locations, closure details and information-zone coordinates. Targets are at most 90 g, 160 g and 420 g for S, M and L, and at least 20 outbound-plus-return cycles. Missing records, placeholder dimensions or a selection unrelated to the proposed directions fail.

For each applicable size, the board's material names, grades, dimensioned flat blank and fold locations agree with the specification. Each board includes assembled views connected intelligibly to its flat patterns. Bag and box materials and construction may differ where the specification assigns different choices; unexplained substitutions, missing folds or conflicting measurements fail.

Read the dimension annotations, with units, for all three sizes. S and M are bags with usable spaces of 300 x 220 x 40 mm and 400 x 300 x 80 mm, and closed external dimensions no greater than 330 x 250 x 50 mm and 430 x 330 x 90 mm. L is a box with usable space of 360 x 240 x 150 mm and closed external dimensions no greater than 380 x 260 x 165 mm. Bag dimensions use width x height x depth; box dimensions use width x depth x height. Smaller external dimensions are acceptable only if the required usable space remains accommodated; omitted sizes, reversed dimension meanings or exceeded limits fail.

Technical measurements establish two separate 100 x 150 mm shipping-label areas, one 60 x 60 mm permanent scan area, an adjacent identifier area with at least 60 x 10 mm usable space, and exactly 20 tally cells measuring at least 8 x 8 mm each on every size. Their locations match the selected coordinates and remain consistent between construction and state views. Scan and identifier interiors remain empty, with their purposes identified by technical annotations. Both seal positions have intelligible indicator fitting and removal sequences. Perspective and temporary label coverage may vary; missing areas, displaced permanent tracking, filled tracking interiors or incomplete seal sequences fail.

The schedule provides exact exterior copy for ROUNDTRIP, REUSABLE MAILER · RETURN ME, Do not discard, the applicable S/M/L letter, SEAL 1 · OUTBOUND, SEAL 2 · RETURN, SCAN, UNIT ID, CYCLE, OUTBOUND and RETURN, with placements. It also records the insert title, all six numbered instructions and both back statements from the client facts, plus the sticker's RETURN, ROUNDTRIP, Seal 2 fitted and one empty checkbox. Locations must distinguish the card's front and back and the sticker's placement beside SEAL 2. Missing text, paraphrased required wording or unspecified placement fails.

The construction boards and each array show the permanent exterior copy specified in the schedule, including the correct size letter, retention reminder, full seal labels, SCAN, UNIT ID and CYCLE. Each array contains closed S and M bags and an L box. The outbound view clearly activates OUTBOUND and its shipping area, with SEAL 1 indicators fitted. The return view activates RETURN and the return label, covers or removes the outbound label, fits SEAL 2 indicators and places the return sticker beside SEAL 2. Both arrays include a contextual arm's-length view in which the active state is readable. Two apparently active shipping labels, incorrect size identification, missing indicators or an ambiguous state fails.

Both sides are shown for a physical 148 x 105 mm card, with all text at least 5 mm inside the trim. The front title is Keep me. Return in me. The ordered instructions are exactly: 1 Open at SEAL 1 and take out your order.; 2 Keep the mailer flat until you decide.; 3 To return, fold the garment and place it inside.; 4 Cover the outbound label and reveal the return label.; 5 Close the mailer and fit the SEAL 2 indicator.; 6 Drop it at any collection point; no box or tape needed. The back reads Not returning anything? Keep the mailer for your next order or hand it in at any store counter. and Designed for many journeys, not one. Line wrapping and typography may vary; omitted, rewritten, reordered or inset-violating text fails.

The standalone sticker establishes a physical 90 x 50 mm design containing the three specified phrases and precisely one unmarked checkbox. The S, M and L return units use that design beside SEAL 2 at the stated physical size, supported by dimensions or a credible scaled application. Perspective may change its apparent shape; altered wording, a different sticker design, a checked or additional checkbox, or incorrect physical sizing fails.

The board shows understandable folding sequences for all three selected constructions, dimensioned final folded forms, a warehouse shelf arrangement and a visibly ten-unit M stack. Folded envelopes do not exceed S 330 x 125 x 15 mm, M 430 x 165 x 25 mm and L 380 x 260 x 40 mm; the stack does not exceed 430 x 165 x 250 mm. Folding supports flat storage without tools. Six customer actions follow the insert's opening, keeping flat, repacking, label change, SEAL 2 fitting and collection-point drop-off order. Smaller compliant envelopes and different shelf compositions are allowed; missing sequences, implausible folds, incorrect stack count or reordered actions fail.

Review the whole video and verify a 12-second runtime. The selected M bag remains recognisable through opening at SEAL 1, flat storage, garment repacking, outbound-label coverage/removal and return-label activation, closure with a fitted SEAL 2 indicator, and return handoff with courier scanning. The sequence agrees with the card and journey board; the last scene may combine drop-off and scanning. Missing actions, a changed bag construction, scanning an unrelated area or a contradictory sequence fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation contains at least 10 pages and names the specification's selected direction on page 1. It visibly incorporates recognisable material from every listed source, including both construction boards, both journey states, both card sides, the sticker and the warehouse arrangement/customer journey. Legible excerpts and reformatted layouts are acceptable when they preserve the selected design and substantive information; merely naming a source, substituting another direction or omitting any source fails.

The presentation explicitly identifies the selected materials consistently with the specification, associates maximum empty mass targets of 90 g, 160 g and 420 g with S, M and L respectively, and states a reuse target of at least 20 cycles. A cycle comprises an outbound and a return journey. Clear equivalent upper-bound wording is allowed; absent values, switched size assignments or treating 20 single journeys as 20 cycles fails.

The presentation states folded size limits of S 330 x 125 x 15 mm, M 430 x 165 x 25 mm and L 380 x 260 x 40 mm, plus the ten-folded-M storage envelope of 430 x 165 x 250 mm. These records agree with the folding board and are identified as storage limits rather than closed shipping dimensions. Missing, conflicting or misassigned limits fail.

The named material grades and depicted folds, joints and fastening mechanisms provide a credible proposal for repeated outbound-and-return use. Recurring opening must not depend on destroying the main enclosure or its primary fastening. Different material families and closure mechanisms are allowed. This judges whether the proposal supports the stated target, not proven laboratory durability; a disposable primary closure or a structurally destructive reuse sequence fails.

Every size has a reusable primary fastening that opens and closes without tools, plus a distinct replaceable tamper-evident indicator at the active journey's seal position. Construction details explain how indicators fit and detach while leaving the unit intact, and the state arrays show the appropriate indicator fitted. Indicator form, material and colour may vary by the selected proposal; a decorative mark without a tamper-evidence mechanism, a tool-dependent closure or damage to the unit during replacement fails.

The customer sequence establishes that a pre-printed return label is supplied inside the unit and is revealed or attached during repacking. The outbound label is covered or cleanly removed without tools, leaving only the return shipping label active in the return array. Either permitted label-change mechanism is acceptable; requiring the customer to obtain or print a new label, leaving competing active labels or damaging the unit fails.

Shipping-label areas are represented as empty zones or blank label placeholders, including when an active return label is depicted. Zone boundaries, technical dimensions and explanatory annotations outside the blank interiors are allowed. Invented addresses, shipping records, barcodes or other populated shipping-label content fail.

The S and M bags and L box retain the selected construction through assembled, journey-state and folded views, allowing the geometric changes required by opening and folding. The family shares an identifiable graphic identity, outbound/return state logic and information-zone system while allowing size-specific bag and box construction. Permanent tracking remains in the selected locations between journeys, with identical required zone dimensions across S, M and L.

Required wording and placement agree with the copy schedule wherever the corresponding card, sticker or packaging feature appears. The applied return stickers reproduce the standalone sticker design, and the customer journey follows the insert card's six actions in order.
